238.title: Grief is love with nowhere left to go
238.content:
When someone we deeply love is no longer with us, the love doesn’t simply disappear.

Hum ab bhi unse baat karna chahte hain, unka khayal rakhna chahte hain, unke saath cheezein baantna chahte hain.

Jo pyaar hum ab bhi mehsoos karte hain aur jo insaan ab pahunch se door hai — un dono ke beech ki khaali jagah ko hi grief kehte hain.

Grief koi problem nahi jise jaldi solve karna hai. Woh pyaar hi hai, bas ab naya roop dhoondh raha hai — ek yaad, ek rasm, unke naam par ek kaam.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Give the love a place: write a letter to the person you miss.
  2. Choose one small ritual in their memory - a song, a dish, a walk.
  3. Let one trusted person know how you are really doing.

Questions women often ask

How long does grief last?

There is no fixed timeline. Grief often softens and returns in waves; be gentle with yourself.

When should I get help for grief?

If grief makes daily life very hard for a long time, or you feel hopeless, please reach out to a counsellor or doctor. In India, Tele-MANAS (14416) is free and available 24x7.

Read next

  • The version of you who survived deserves thanks, not judgement
  • Your body kept the score

236.title: The child inside you is still waiting to hear: it was not your fault
236.content:
Healing begins with a powerful affirmation: “I am free from the weight of blame.”

Bachpan mein jo hua, uska bojh kai baar hum badi umar tak uthate rehte hain — jaise galti hamari hi thi.

Aapke andar ki woh chhoti bachchi abhi bhi masoomiyat se chamakti hai. Use bas woh sunna hai jo shayad kisi ne kabhi kaha nahi: “yeh tumhari galti nahi thi.”

Aaj use yeh khud kahiye. Healing wahin se shuru hoti hai jahan blame khatam hota hai.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Find a childhood photo and look at it for a minute.
  2. Say or write to her: “It was not your fault.”
  3. Notice one belief you still carry from that time, and question it gently.

Questions women often ask

What is inner child healing?

Gently revisiting feelings and beliefs formed in childhood, and offering yourself the understanding you needed then.

Can coaching help with childhood trauma?

Coaching can help with present patterns. Deep childhood trauma is best worked through with a qualified therapist - Shashi will say so honestly if that is what you need.

Read next

  • The version of you who survived deserves thanks, not judgement
  • Your body kept the score

234.title: You cannot heal in the environment that keeps hurting you
234.content:
Sometimes, choosing peace means choosing distance.

Ek ghaav ko bharne ke liye use baar-baar chhoona band karna padta hai. Mann ke ghaav bhi aise hi hote hain.

Agar wahi log, wahi baatein, wahi mahaul har baar chot ko taaza kar dete hain, toh sirf “strong” rehne se healing nahi hogi.

Doori hamesha rishta todna nahi hoti. Kam milna, kuch topics par baat na karna, apne liye alag jagah banana — yeh bhi doori hai. Peace chuniye. Behtar chuniye. Khud ko chuniye.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Notice which people, places or conversations reopen the same hurt.
  2. Choose one kind of distance you can create - time, topics or space.
  3. Fill that space with something that helps you heal.

Questions women often ask

Does choosing distance mean I don't love them?

No. Distance can protect a relationship as well as you - it gives the wound time to heal.

What if I can't leave the environment?

Then create small distances inside it: boundaries on topics, time for yourself, and support from people outside.

Read next

  • A boundary is not a punishment
  • Some people are lessons

232.title: Start the day answering to yourself
232.content:
A strong mindset begins when you stop leaving yourself last.

Hum din bhar sabke sawaalon ka jawab dete hain — ghar, kaam, phone. Par apne sawaalon ka jawab dena bhool jaate hain.

Teen sawaal kaafi hain: Aaj mujhe kya chahiye? Main kya mehsoos kar rahi hoon? Mere liye sach mein kya zaroori hai?

Jab aap pehle khud se baat karti hain, din aapka hota hai — warna din sabka hota hai, aur aap bas usme fit hoti rehti hain.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Before checking messages, write three answers: what do I need, what do I feel, what matters?
  2. Pick one need and plan when you will meet it today.
  3. At night, check in: did I keep that one promise to myself?

Questions women often ask

What is a morning check-in?

A few quiet minutes to notice your needs, feelings and priorities before the world's demands arrive.

Why do I always put myself last?

Often because we learned that being good means being available to everyone first. Noticing that pattern is the first step to changing it.

Read next

  • You are allowed to change the rules
  • The version of you who survived deserves thanks, not judgement

230.title: Healthy love feels like…
230.content:
Healthy love is not just saying “I love you”.

Clarity — mujhe pata hai main is rishte mein kahan khadi hoon. Consistency — baatein aur kaam kuch din nahi, roz ek jaise rehte hain.

Emotional safety — main apni feelings bina judge, insult ya reject hone ke dar ke keh sakti hoon. Mutual efforts — rishta ek insaan ke kandhon par nahi chalta.

Healthy love shor nahi karta, sukoon deta hai.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Score your relationship from 1 to 5 on clarity, consistency, emotional safety and mutual effort.
  2. Share the score that matters most with your partner - calmly, with one example.
  3. Agree on one small action together.

Questions women often ask

What does healthy love feel like?

Clear, consistent, emotionally safe, and built by both people - calm more often than chaotic.

Is intense love the same as healthy love?

Not always. Intensity can feel exciting, but healthy love usually feels steady and safe.

Read next

  • Not every silence needs an explanation
  • You are not a backup plan

228.title: You cannot step into a new chapter while holding on to the old one
228.content:
Sometimes, moving forward simply means putting down what no longer belongs in your next chapter.

Purani galtiyan, purane beliefs, toxic rishte, “log kya kahenge” — hum inhe ek bojh ki tarah saath le kar chalte rehte hain, aur phir sochte hain ki naya shuru kyun nahi ho raha.

Naye chapter mein kadam rakhne ke liye pehle haath khaali karne padte hain. Iska matlab purana bhool jaana nahi — bas use ab saath le kar na chalna.

Aaj ek cheez chuniye jo aapke agle chapter ka hissa nahi hai. Use dheere se neeche rakh dijiye.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. List what you are still carrying from the last chapter - regrets, beliefs, other people's opinions.
  2. Mark one thing that doesn't belong in your next chapter.
  3. Decide one action that puts it down - a conversation, a goodbye, or simply a decision.

Questions women often ask

How do I let go of the past?

Letting go is less a single moment and more a daily choice not to pick the old weight up again. Start with one thing, not everything.

Does moving on mean forgetting?

No. You can honour what happened and still stop carrying it into every new day.

Read next

  • Some people are lessons
  • You are allowed to change the rules

226.title: Everything looks fine — so why do I still feel empty?
226.content:
You don’t have to figure everything out alone.

Achha parivaar, stable career, achhe dost, aaram ki cheezein — sab kuch hai. Phir bhi andar kuch khaali sa lagta hai, aur hum is ehsaas ko “ungrateful” samajh kar dabaa dete hain.

Yeh khaalipan kamzori nahi, ek signal hai — ki kahin na kahin aap apni needs, apne sapno ya apni awaaz se door ho gayi hain.

Ise akele samajhna zaroori nahi. Sahi guidance, sachchi baatcheet aur ek supportive community se safar halka ho jaata hai. Agla chapter ek chhote faisle se shuru ho sakta hai — khud ko chunne se.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Write down what “fine” looks like in your life - and then what feels missing.
  2. Notice which of your own needs or dreams you have not spoken of in a long time.
  3. Share the feeling with one person you trust, or in a safe community.

Questions women often ask

Is it wrong to feel empty when life looks good?

No. Feeling empty is not ingratitude - it is a signal that something important to you is being left out.

When should I seek professional help for feeling empty?

If the emptiness lasts for weeks, affects your sleep, appetite or daily life, or comes with hopelessness, please speak to a doctor or mental health professional. Coaching is not a replacement for that care.

Read next

  • Your body kept the score
  • Softness is not weakness

224.title: Missing someone is not a reason to go back
224.content:
Missing them is a feeling. Going back is a decision.

Kabhi-kabhi hum kisi ko miss karte hain, lekin iska matlab yeh nahi ki humein wahi rishta ya wahi situation wapas chahiye.

Aap yaadon ko miss kar sakti hain, aur phir bhi apni peace chun sakti hain.

Woh chuniye jo aapki peace ko bachaaye — woh nahi jo purana ghaav phir se khol de. Kuch chapters band hone ke liye hote hain, dohraane ke liye nahi.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. When you miss them, write down what exactly you miss - the person, a feeling, or a memory.
  2. Next to it, write why you left.
  3. Do one thing that gives you that feeling in a healthier way.

Questions women often ask

Why do I miss someone who hurt me?

Because the mind remembers the good moments and the familiar. Missing them is natural; it doesn't mean the relationship was right.

How do I stop going back to an ex?

Treat missing as a feeling to sit with, not an instruction. Lean on friends, limit contact and remember why you chose peace.

Read next

  • Some people are lessons
  • Change feels like loss before it feels like freedom

222.title: Stop shrinking to fit rooms you have already outgrown
222.content:
You don’t need to become smaller to be accepted.

Kabhi-kabhi hum acceptance ke liye apni needs, sapne aur awaaz chhoti kar dete hain.

Par jo jagah aapko chhota karke hi rakh sakti hai, woh aapki jagah nahi rahi.

Agar koi space aapki growth ko limit kar raha hai, shayad waqt hai aisi jagah chunne ka jahan aap badh sakein, saans le sakein aur khud ho sakein.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Notice where you make yourself smaller - quieter, less ambitious, less visible.
  2. Ask: who or what am I shrinking for?
  3. Take up a little more space this week: speak up once, share one dream.

Questions women often ask

Why do I make myself smaller around others?

Often to stay accepted or avoid conflict. It works for a while, but it costs you your voice.

How do I know I've outgrown a space?

When staying requires you to shrink your needs, dreams or voice, the space may no longer fit who you are becoming.

Read next

  • You are not a backup plan
  • You are allowed to change the rules

220.title: You don’t need to reopen the wound to prove it hurt
220.content:
You already know what you went through.

Kabhi-kabhi hum dard ko baar-baar yaad karte hain, sunaate hain, dohraate hain — jaise uske bina koi maanega hi nahi ki humein chot lagi thi.

Aapka anubhav sach tha, chahe aap use roz na dohraayein. Use sach saabit karne ke liye ghaav ko khula rakhna zaroori nahi.

Healing ka matlab yeh bhi ho sakta hai — wapas na jaana. Kahani ko yaad rakhiye, par usme rehna band kijiye.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Notice when you retell a painful story - and ask what you hope to get from retelling it.
  2. Write the story once, fully, then close the notebook.
  3. Replace one retelling with one kind act for yourself.

Questions women often ask

Is talking about past pain bad?

No. Speaking about pain can heal. The difference is between processing it and reliving it again and again without relief.

How do I stop reliving painful memories?

Start by noticing the trigger, then gently bring yourself back to the present. If memories overwhelm you, a trained professional can help.

Read next

  • Your body kept the score
  • You don’t have to keep carrying the armor

218.title: Green flags to look for in a relationship
218.content:
Not every healthy relationship is perfect.

Hum red flags pehchaanna seekh lete hain, par green flags ke baare mein kam sochte hain.

Asli green flags: izzat, emotional safety, consistency, aur jhagde ke baad rishta jodne ki koshish. Chhote vaade nibhaana, aur asehmati mein bhi shaant rehna.

Aisa rishta chuniye jahan shaanti naturally mehsoos ho — kabhi-kabhi nahi.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. List the green flags you see in your closest relationship.
  2. Notice which ones you also offer in return.
  3. Appreciate one green flag out loud this week.

Questions women often ask

What are green flags in a relationship?

Respect, emotional safety, consistency, keeping small promises, staying calm in disagreement and repairing after conflict.

Does a healthy relationship have no fights?

No. Healthy couples still disagree - what matters is that they repair afterwards.

Read next

  • Not every silence needs an explanation
  • You are not a backup plan

216.title: Small and consistent beats big and occasional
216.content:
The version of you that you want is not built in one dramatic weekend. It is built in unremarkable Tuesdays.

Hum badlav ko ek bade din ki tarah dekhte hain — naya saal, naya Monday, ek dramatic decision.

Par asli badlav saadharan dinon mein hota hai — jab kuch khaas nahi ho raha, phir bhi aap apna chhota sa vaada nibhaati hain.

Aadat ka sabse chhota version chuniye aur use pakad ke rakhiye. Aapka sabse chhota agla kadam kya hai?

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Pick one habit you want and shrink it to two minutes.
  2. Attach it to something you already do every day.
  3. Track it for seven days - never skip twice in a row.

Questions women often ask

Why do my big resolutions fail?

Big changes depend on motivation, which comes and goes. Small habits survive ordinary days.

How long does it take to build a habit?

It varies from person to person. Focus on showing up consistently rather than counting days.

Read next

  • “Why me?” keeps you stuck. “What now?” moves you forward
  • You are allowed to change the rules

214.title: Khud ko sambhalna selfishness nahi hai
214.content:
Apne liye time nikalna bhi self-respect hai.

Hum mein se kai women ko sikhaya gaya ki apne liye waqt nikalna swaarth hai — pehle sab, phir main.

Par jab aap apna khayal rakhti hain, aap Bhagwan ki sabse khoobsurat rachna ka khayal rakh rahi hoti hain — aur phir har us cheez ke liye behtar maujood hoti hain jo aapke liye maayne rakhti hai.

Exercise, neend, ek shaant cup chai, ek “nahi” — self-care inhi chhoti chhoti cheezon se banta hai.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Choose one 20-minute slot this week that is only for you.
  2. Put it in your calendar like any other promise.
  3. When guilt comes, remind yourself: caring for myself helps me care for others.

Questions women often ask

Is self-care selfish?

No. Self-care keeps you well enough to show up for the people and the work you care about.

What counts as self-care?

Anything that genuinely restores you - rest, movement, quiet, a boundary, time with people who feel safe.

Read next

  • Softness is not weakness
  • A boundary is not a punishment

212.title: Stop calling it rejection — sometimes it’s redirection
212.content:
What didn’t work out may be making space for what will.

Jab koi rishta, naukri ya mauka haath se nikal jaata hai, dil kehta hai — “main kaafi nahi thi.”

Par jo dard rejection jaisa lagta hai, woh kai baar ek mod hota hai — growth, peace, self-love aur naye mauko ki taraf.

Dard ko maaniye, use jaldi se positive mat banaiye. Phir ek sawaal poochhiye: is band darwaaze ne meri zindagi mein kis cheez ke liye jagah banayi hai?

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Write what you lost - and let yourself feel it without rushing.
  2. Next to it, write one thing this ending made space for.
  3. Take one step towards that new space this week.

Questions women often ask

How do I stop taking rejection personally?

Remember that a “no” often says more about fit, timing or the other person's capacity than about your worth.

Is it okay to still feel hurt?

Yes. Seeing it as redirection doesn't mean skipping the pain. Feel it first; the new direction gets clearer after.

Read next

  • Some people are lessons
  • Change feels like loss before it feels like freedom

210.title: Peacekeeping is not peace
210.content:
Keeping everyone comfortable by disappearing is not harmony. It is a quiet form of absence.

Ghar mein sab khush rahein, isliye aap chup reh jaati hain. Har jhagde ko aap apne andar sokh leti hain — family ki “shock absorber”.

Bahar se lagta hai sab shaant hai. Par jis shaanti mein aap khud hi gayab hain, woh peace nahi, peacekeeping hai — aur uski keemat aap chuka rahi hain.

Asli shaanti mein aap bhi kamre mein maujood hoti hain — apni awaaz aur apni zaroorton ke saath.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Notice one moment this week where you stay silent only to keep the peace.
  2. Say one honest sentence instead - calmly, starting with “I”.
  3. Notice that the room survives your voice.

Questions women often ask

Is avoiding conflict the same as keeping the peace?

No. Avoiding conflict by silencing yourself only moves the cost onto you. Real peace includes your needs too.

How do I stop being the family's shock absorber?

Start small: share one feeling, set one boundary, and let others hold some of the discomfort instead of you.

Read next

  • A boundary is not a punishment
  • You are not responsible for how everyone feels about your honesty

208.title: Love is not enough on its own
208.content:
Healthy relationships need respect, effort, trust and emotional safety.

Hum maan lete hain ki agar pyaar hai, toh sab theek ho jayega. Par pyaar ek beej hai — use paudha banne ke liye roz paani chahiye.

Izzat, koshish, bharosa aur emotional safety — yahi woh paani hai. Inke bina sabse gehra pyaar bhi sookhne lagta hai.

Pyaar tabhi khoobsurat hai, jab dono use nurture karein.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Rate your relationship on four things: respect, effort, trust, emotional safety.
  2. Pick the lowest one and name one small action that would nurture it.
  3. Talk about it calmly with your partner, starting with “I feel…”.

Questions women often ask

If we love each other, why is it so hard?

Because love is the feeling; respect, effort and safety are the daily practice that keeps it alive.

What makes a relationship emotionally safe?

Being able to share feelings without fear of insult, judgement or rejection - and knowing conflict will be repaired.

Read next

  • Not every silence needs an explanation
  • You are not a backup plan

206.title: Healing is not becoming someone new
206.content:
It’s returning to yourself.

Kabhi-kabhi life ke anubhavon ke baad hum apni hi needs, sapno aur pehchaan se door ho jaate hain.

Healing ka matlab perfect banna nahi hai. Iska matlab hai dheere-dheere us insaan se dobara judna jo aap thi — us se pehle jab aapne maan liya tha ki aapko koi aur banna padega.

Aapko naya banne ki zaroorat nahi. Bas khud ke paas wapas aana hai.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Write down three things you loved doing before life got heavy.
  2. Do one of them this week, even for ten minutes.
  3. Notice what part of “you” it brings back.

Questions women often ask

What does healing actually mean?

Not becoming perfect or new, but slowly reconnecting with your own needs, dreams and identity.

How do I know I am healing?

Often it shows quietly: you react less, rest more, and recognise yourself again.

Read next

  • You don’t have to keep carrying the armor
  • The version of you who survived deserves thanks, not judgement

204.title: Protect the first hour
204.content:
Your first hour is not selfish. It’s self-leadership.

Aap din kaise shuru karti hain, aksar wahi tay karta hai ki baaki din aap kaise jeeti hain.

Aankh khulte hi phone, sabke messages, sabki zarooratein — aur khud ki baari aate-aate din khatam ho jaata hai.

Pehla ghanta apne liye rakhiye: thoda paani, thodi saans, thoda likhna. Baaki sab us bache hue waqt mein adjust ho jaata hai — aur aap zyada shaant hokar sabke liye maujood hoti hain.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Keep your phone away for the first 20 minutes after waking.
  2. Drink water, breathe slowly and ask: what do I need today?
  3. Write one line of intention before you open any message.

Questions women often ask

Is it selfish to take time for myself in the morning?

No. Your first hour is self-leadership - when you start steady, you show up better for everyone else.

What if I have no time in the morning?

Start with five minutes. The habit matters more than the length - protect a small slot first, then grow it.

Read next

  • “Why me?” keeps you stuck. “What now?” moves you forward
  • Softness is not weakness

202.title: You are not too much
202.content:
Sometimes you simply gave your heart to someone who didn’t have the capacity to give the same in return.

“Main zyada expect karti hoon.” “Shayad main hi too much hoon.” Ek adhoore rishte ke baad hum aksar khud ko hi chhota kar lete hain.

Kabhi-kabhi baat aapki zaroorton ki nahi hoti, saamne wale ki kshamta ki hoti hai. Pyaar, dhyaan aur izzat chahna “too much” nahi hai.

Kisi aur ki seemaon mein fit hone ke liye khud ko kabhi chhota mat kijiye.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Write down the needs you were told were “too much”.
  2. Next to each, ask: is this a fair need in a healthy relationship?
  3. Keep the fair ones, and let go of the guilt attached to them.

Questions women often ask

How do I stop feeling like I'm “too much”?

Separate your needs from someone's capacity to meet them. Wanting care and respect is normal; not everyone can give it.

Should I lower my expectations in relationships?

Lower unrealistic ones, not basic ones. Respect, consistency and emotional safety are not too much to ask.

Read next

  • You are not a backup plan
  • Not every silence needs an explanation

200.title: Like a butterfly, you have to leave the cocoon behind
200.content:
Growth begins when you dare to leave what once felt safe.

Cocoon butterfly ki dushman nahi thi. Wahi jagah thi jahan woh surakshit rahi, jahan uska badalna shuru hua.

Hamari zindagi mein bhi kuch aadatein, rishte aur soch aisi hi hoti hain — ek waqt par unhone humein bachaya. Par jo jagah kabhi safe thi, zaroori nahi ki aaj bhi wahi aapke liye sahi ho.

Bahar nikalna dar lagta hai, kyunki naya abhi jaana-pehchana nahi hai. Khud par bharosa rakhiye, aur us zindagi ke liye jagah banaiye jiski aap hakdaar hain.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Name one “cocoon” in your life - a habit, belief or situation that once kept you safe.
  2. Ask: is it still protecting me, or only keeping me small?
  3. Take one small step outside it this week, and notice what you feel.

Questions women often ask

Why does growth feel so scary?

Because it asks you to leave the familiar before the new feels safe. That fear is normal - it doesn't mean you are going the wrong way.

How do I know it's time to move on from something?

When something that once protected you now mostly holds you back - keeping you quiet, small or stuck - it may have done its job.

Read next

  • Change feels like loss before it feels like freedom
  • You don’t have to keep carrying the armor

106.title: You don’t have to keep carrying the armor
106.content:
Fear can protect you from getting hurt — and also protect you from being truly alive.

Jo deewar aapne kabhi khud ko bachane ke liye banayi thi, wo galat nahi thi. Us waqt shayad wahi sahi tha — kisi pe zyada bharosa na karna, sab kuch akele sambhalna, har baat pehle se soch lena.

Lekin jo cheez past mein aapko protect karti thi, wahi aaj aapko rok bhi sakti hai. Armor chot se bachata hai — par kisi ko aapke kareeb bhi nahi aane deta.

Healing ka matlab armor phenk dena nahi hai. Healing hai ye pehchanna ki kab use utaarna safe hai — aur kis ke saamne.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. List the rules you made to stay safe - never ask for help, always stay in control.
  2. Ask of each one: is this still protecting me, or only keeping people out?
  3. Lower one piece of armor with one safe person this week.

Questions women often ask

How do I know if I’m emotionally guarded?

Common signs are finding it hard to ask for help, expecting to be let down, and feeling safer handling everything alone. None of these are flaws - they are old protection that may have outlived its job.

How do you start healing from past hurt?

Start by recognising what your defences once did for you, with gratitude rather than blame. Healing is learning when it is safe to let go - at your own pace.

Read next

  • Your body kept the score
  • Change feels like loss before it feels like freedom

108.title: Change feels like loss before it feels like freedom
108.content:
Sometimes letting go is not losing yourself — it’s finally choosing yourself.

Expectations, people pleasing, “log kya kahenge” — inhe chhodna aasaan nahi lagta. Kyunki ye sirf aadatein nahi hain, saalon se ye aapki pehchaan ka hissa rahi hain.

Isliye jab aap badalna shuru karti hain, pehle azaadi nahi, khaali-pan mehsoos hota hai. Lagta hai kuch kho gaya hai.

Wo ehsaas galat nahi hai — wo bas beech ka raasta hai. Jo jagah khaali hui hai, wahi dheere-dheere aapki apni jagah banegi.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Name one old habit you are trying to let go of.
  2. When the empty feeling comes, call it what it is: the middle of change, not the end.
  3. Fill that space with one small thing that is truly yours.

Questions women often ask

Why does positive change feel so uncomfortable?

Old habits, even unhelpful ones, feel familiar and safe. Giving them up can feel like loss before the new way feels like home - that discomfort is normal.

How long does it take to feel better after a big change?

There is no fixed timeline. For most people it eases as new habits become familiar, and support from a coach or a community can make the middle stretch less lonely.

110.title: The version of you who survived deserves thanks, not judgement
110.content:
Be proud of the woman who kept going.

Hum aksar apne purane version ko judge karte hain — “maine itna kyun saha?”, “pehle kyun nahi samjhi?”

Par us waqt aapke paas jitni samajh thi, jitni himmat thi, aapne usi se kaam chalaya. Aapne sirf survive nahi kiya — aapne khud ko sambhala, seekha aur grow kiya.

Aaj jo aap jaanti hain, wo usi ki wajah se jaanti hain. Use thoda credit dijiye. Wo deserve karti hai.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Write down three things your past self got through.
  2. Next to each, write what she learned - not what she got wrong.
  3. Read it once, and say thank you to her.

Questions women often ask

How do I stop judging my past self?

Remember that you made choices with the understanding and strength you had then. What you know today, you know because she lived through it.

What is self-compassion?

Treating yourself with the same kindness you would give a close friend going through a hard time - honest, but gentle.

Read next

  • Softness is not weakness
  • You don’t have to keep carrying the armor

112.title: Not every silence needs an explanation
112.content:
Sometimes the healthiest thing you can do is stop assuming.

Message ka reply nahi aaya, aur dimaag kahaniyan banane lagta hai — “kya main enough nahi hoon?”, “kya wo naraz hai?”, “kya maine kuch galat kaha?”

Zyada tar baar silence ka matlab rejection nahi hota. Saamne wala thaka hua ho sakta hai, busy ho sakta hai, ya bas apne aap mein ho sakta hai.

Har chuppi ko assumptions se mat bhariye. Logon ko space dijiye — aur khud ko peace.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. When a silence starts a story in your head, write the story down.
  2. Next to it, write two other explanations that are just as possible.
  3. Choose one calming action - a walk, a call to a friend - instead of sending another message.

Questions women often ask

How do I stop overthinking when someone doesn’t reply?

Notice the story your mind is building and treat it as a guess, not a fact. Give it time, and if it matters, ask directly and calmly rather than assuming.

Is silence in a relationship always a bad sign?

No. People go quiet for many reasons - tiredness, stress, needing space. Silence used again and again as punishment is different, and worth talking about openly.

Read next

  • You are not a backup plan
  • A boundary is not a punishment

114.title: You are allowed to change the rules
114.content:
What you believed years ago may not be what you need today.

“Achhi ladki aisa nahi karti.” “Pehle sabka khayal, phir apna.” Kuch rules humne tab maan liye the jab humare paas koi aur option nahi tha.

Wo rules us waqt survive karne ke liye the. Par jo kabhi zaroori tha, zaroori nahi ki aaj bhi wahi aapke liye sahi ho.

Aap ab zyada jaanti hain. Aap grow kar chuki hain. Aap dobara choose kar sakti hain — aur alag choose kar sakti hain.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Write down one rule you grew up with - “achhi ladki…”, “pehle sab, phir main”.
  2. Ask: who gave me this rule, and does it still serve me?
  3. Rewrite it in your own words, as a rule you choose to live by.

Questions women often ask

What are limiting beliefs?

Old ideas about yourself or life - often learned early - that quietly decide what you think you are allowed to do. Noticing them is the first step to changing them.

Can you really change beliefs as an adult?

Yes. Beliefs are learned, so they can be re-examined. Coaching helps you notice them, question them and practise new choices until they feel natural.

Read next

  • “Why me?” keeps you stuck. “What now?” moves you forward
  • Change feels like loss before it feels like freedom

116.title: “Why me?” keeps you stuck. “What now?” moves you forward
116.content:
Life becomes lighter when you stop asking why it happened and start asking what you can do next.

“Mere saath hi kyun?” — ye sawaal bilkul natural hai. Dard mein sabse pehle yahi aata hai.

Mushkil tab hoti hai jab hum isi sawaal mein ruk jaate hain. Iska koi jawab nahi milta, aur hum wahin khade reh jaate hain.

“Ab kya?” ek chhota sa shift hai. Ye dard ko chhota nahi karta — bas aapka agla kadam aapke haath mein wapas de deta hai.

Ye thought pehle Instagram par share hua tha.

Try this today

  1. Catch yourself the next time you ask “why me?” - no judgement.
  2. Replace it with “what now?” and write one small answer.
  3. Do that one thing within 24 hours, however small.

Questions women often ask

Why do I keep asking “why me?”

It is a natural response to pain - the mind looks for a reason. The trouble starts when the question has no answer and keeps you standing in the same place.

How do I change my mindset after a setback?

Move the question from the past to the next step. Small, doable actions rebuild a sense of control faster than waiting to feel ready.

Read next

  • You are allowed to change the rules
  • The version of you who survived deserves thanks, not judgement

34.title: You are not responsible for how everyone feels about your honesty
34.content:
Say the true thing kindly, then let it land where it lands.

Sach bolna aur uske baad saamne wale ka mood sambhalna — ye do alag kaam hain. Hum aksar dono apne sar le lete hain.

Aapka kaam hai sach ko narmi se kehna. Uske baad wo baat unke paas hai, aapke paas nahi.

Isi ek farq se bahut si mushkil baatein aasaan ho jaati hain.

Agar ye aapki baat lag rahi hai, ek free demo session par baat karte hain — WhatsApp par message kijiye.

Try this today

  1. Notice the moment you start softening the truth just to keep someone comfortable.
  2. Say it once, kindly and clearly - no over-explaining.
  3. Let their reaction belong to them. Breathe, and don’t rush in to fix it.

Questions women often ask

How do I stop people-pleasing?

Start small. Say one honest “no” this week in a low-stakes situation and notice that you survive the discomfort. People-pleasing loosens through practice, not through one big decision.

Is it unkind to say something that might hurt?

Kindness is in how you say it, not in hiding it. You can be gentle and truthful at the same time - what hurts more over time is a relationship built on things left unsaid.

Read next

  • A boundary is not a punishment
  • Softness is not weakness

33.title: Softness is not weakness
33.content:
It takes strength to stay open after being hurt.

Chot lagne ke baad band ho jaana aasaan hai. Deewar bana lena aasaan hai.

Mushkil hai — chot khane ke baad bhi naram rehna. Bharosa dobara karna, jaante hue ki dobara dukh ho sakta hai.

Wo kamzori nahi. Wo sabse badi taakat hai jo main apne clients mein dekhti hoon.

Agar ye aapki baat lag rahi hai, ek free demo session par baat karte hain — WhatsApp par message kijiye.

Try this today

  1. Notice one place where you have gone hard to avoid getting hurt again.
  2. Allow one small soft thing today - ask for help, rest, or say how you feel.
  3. Remind yourself: rest is not giving up. It is how you restore yourself.

Questions women often ask

Is it weak to show emotions?

No. Showing emotions with awareness is a strength - it takes courage to stay open when you know you might be hurt again.

How can strong women make space for rest?

Treat rest as part of the work, not a reward after it. You do not have to handle everything every day to be strong.

Read next

  • The version of you who survived deserves thanks, not judgement
  • You are not responsible for how everyone feels about your honesty

32.title: Some people are lessons
32.content:
Not lifetimes.

Har rishta nibhane ke liye nahi hota. Kuch sirf kuch sikhane ke liye aate hain.

Dikkat tab hoti hai jab hum lesson ko lifetime banane ki koshish karte hain — sirf isliye ki chhodna haar jaisa lagta hai.

Chhodna haar nahi hai. Kabhi-kabhi wahi sabse samajhdaari wala kadam hota hai.

Agar ye aapki baat lag rahi hai, ek free demo session par baat karte hain — WhatsApp par message kijiye.

Try this today

  1. Name what this relationship taught you - one line is enough.
  2. Separate the lesson from the person: you keep the first, you can release the second.
  3. Notice where you are holding on only because leaving feels like losing.

Questions women often ask

How do I let go of someone I still love?

Loving someone and staying with them are two different decisions. You can honour what was real and still choose what is healthy for you now. Letting go is usually a process, not a moment.

Is ending a relationship a failure?

No. Leaving is not failing, and staying is not loyalty. Sometimes the wisest step is recognising that a chapter has done its work.

  • You are not a backup plan

31.title: Your body kept the score
31.content:
Long after your mind said it was fine.

Mann kehta hai “ho gaya, aage badh gaye.” Par neend nahi aati, kandhe akde rehte hain, aur kisi ki ek line se poora din bhaari ho jaata hai.

Sharir jhooth nahi bolta. Wo yaad rakhta hai jo mann jaldi bhoolna chahta hai.

Isliye healing sirf sochne se nahi hoti. Use mehsoos karna bhi padta hai — aur uske liye ek safe jagah chahiye.

Agar ye aapki baat lag rahi hai, ek free demo session par baat karte hain — WhatsApp par message kijiye.

Try this today

  1. Pause twice a day and notice where you feel tension - jaw, shoulders, stomach.
  2. Breathe slowly into that spot for one minute, without trying to fix anything.
  3. Write one line about what that feeling might be carrying.

Questions women often ask

Can unresolved emotions show up in the body?

Many people notice stress as tight shoulders, poor sleep or a heavy stomach long after a painful time has passed. Paying attention to these signals is a first step - and if symptoms persist, please see a doctor.

Is coaching the same as therapy for emotional pain?

No. Coaching works on your present - thoughts, patterns, relationships - and on what you can do next. If you need clinical or therapeutic support, Shashi will tell you honestly and point you to the right professional.

  • You don’t have to keep carrying the armor
  • The version of you who survived deserves thanks, not judgement

30.title: You are not a backup plan
30.content:
Stop auditioning for a place you already belong.

Agar aapko baar-baar khud ko saabit karna pad raha hai — to sawaal aap par nahi, us jagah par hai.

Audition tab tak chalta hai jab tak aap maante hain ki jagah aapko milni baaki hai. Jis din aap maan leti hain ki jagah aapki thi hi, audition apne aap band ho jaata hai.

Ye sochne ki baat hai: aap kis rishte mein abhi bhi apni jagah kama rahi hain?

Agar ye aapki baat lag rahi hai, ek free demo session par baat karte hain — WhatsApp par message kijiye.

Try this today

  1. Write down what you keep doing to “earn” your place with this person.
  2. Ask honestly: would I accept this if a friend described it to me?
  3. Choose one thing you will stop over-giving this week - and notice what changes.

Questions women often ask

How do I know if I’m someone’s second choice?

Look at patterns, not promises: who makes plans, who waits, who explains. If you are always the one adjusting, you are carrying the relationship alone.

How can I stop seeking validation in relationships?

Begin by giving yourself what you keep asking others for - time, respect, rest. When your worth is not on the table every day, you stop auditioning for it.

Read next

  • Some people are lessons
  • Not every silence needs an explanation

29.title: A boundary is not a punishment
29.content:
It is a doorway that tells people how to love you well.

Bahut si women ke liye boundary ka matlab hota hai jhagda. Isliye wo boundary banati hi nahi — sochti hain ki rishta bigad jayega.

Par boundary rishta todti nahi. Wo batati hai ki rishta kaise chal sakta hai. “Mujhe raat 10 baje ke baad kaam ki baat nahi karni” — ye dushmani nahi hai. Ye ek darwaza hai jispar likha hai ki andar kaise aana hai.

Jo log aapse sach mein pyaar karte hain, unke liye ye raahat hoti hai. Unhe andaza lagana band karna padta hai.

Agar ye aapki baat lag rahi hai, ek free demo session par baat karte hain — WhatsApp par message kijiye.

Try this today

  1. Pick one situation that keeps draining you - a call, a request, a habit.
  2. Say your boundary in one calm sentence, without a long explanation: “Main 9 baje ke baad calls nahi le paungi.”
  3. Then act on it the same way every time. Your “no” becomes real when your actions match it.

Questions women often ask

Is setting a boundary selfish?

No. A boundary tells people what you can give and what you cannot. It protects the relationship from quiet resentment, which does far more damage than an honest “no”.

What if people get upset when I set a boundary?

Some will, at first - especially those who benefited from you having none. Stay kind and stay consistent. Their discomfort is not proof that you were wrong.
